_note: Single source of definitions for every parameter and metric. The UI reads this for its info popovers and the README is generated against it, so a definition cannot drift between the two. Edit here, nowhere else.

n_sources.label: sources
n_sources.short: How many sources are in the ring.
n_sources.long: Odd counts are preferred. With an even ring every source has one directly opposite it, and those antipodal pairs are exactly what cancels when the ring is coherent.

rotation_deg_per_sec.label: ring rate
rotation_deg_per_sec.short: How fast the ring of sources circulates.
rotation_deg_per_sec.long: Under the analytic HRTF a full 360 deg lap reads as left-right oscillation at twice the rate, because there is no front-back discrimination. Rate and direction are therefore confounded right now; source count and coherence are not.

start_azimuths.label: azimuths
start_azimuths.short: Explicit starting position of each source.
start_azimuths.long: 0 is straight ahead and positive is to the right. Uneven spacing is one of the three ways to break the ring's symmetry, and it works even with fully coherent sources.

spacing_deg.label: spacing
spacing_deg.short: Constant gap between sources, as an alternative to listing azimuths.
spacing_deg.long: Leave unset for sources spread evenly over the full 360 deg.

offset_deg.label: offset
offset_deg.short: Rotates the whole ring's starting position.
offset_deg.long: Does not change the geometry, only where it starts. Useful for placing a gap in an uneven ring behind rather than in front.

per_source_gain_db.label: per-source gain
per_source_gain_db.long: The third documented way to break ring symmetry, alongside decorrelation and uneven spacing. Works on a fully coherent ring.

amount.label: decorrelation
amount.short: Master coherence knob. 0 is identical copies, 1 is maximally decorrelated.
amount.long: The main symmetry break. At 0 a symmetric ring collapses to a dead-centre mono image with no interaural information at all, and rotating it changes nothing. Level is held constant across the whole sweep, so this changes coherence only.

per_source_amount.label: per-source amount
per_source_amount.short: Decorrelation amount for each source separately.
per_source_amount.long: Setting one source to 0 inside an otherwise diffuse bed is the coherence hotspot. Note the coherent source then travels with the ring: for coherence that moves independently of the sources, use the hotspot controls instead.

family.label: family
family.short: How the decorrelating filter is built: velvet, allpass, or none.
family.long: Velvet is sparse plus/minus 1 impulses on a jittered grid, near-colourless. Allpass is flat magnitude with scrambled phase, which smears transients more. These are two points on one continuum rather than two categories: velvet converges on allpass once density passes roughly 400 impulses/sec.

ir_ms.label: IR length
ir_ms.short: Length of the decorrelating impulse response, so how far the signal is smeared in time.
ir_ms.long: The filter-shape control with the most headroom: inter-source coherence runs about 0.19 down to 0.04 across 5 to 120 ms, which is large compared to the roughly 0.05 measurement noise. Prefer sweeping this over density.

density.label: density
density.short: How many impulses fill the velvet IR.
density.long: Only does work while sparse. Below about 400 impulses/sec each step matters a lot; above it the IR is already noise-like and further density is inert, changing coherence by less than the measurement noise.

phase_depth.label: phase depth
phase_depth.short: How far the allpass filter scrambles phase, from identity to full.
phase_depth.long: Partial scrambling is a continuous axis rather than the on/off the prefabs implied. At 0 there is no decorrelation at all.

envelope.label: IR envelope
envelope.short: Amplitude shape over the IR: flat, hann, or decay.
envelope.long: Was a hidden variable in the prefabs, which differed in window as well as density. It dominates in the sparse regime, where a flat envelope leaves the forced direct tap at full amplitude and keeps the source coherent with its own dry signal, and is nearly inert once the IR is dense. Hold it fixed when comparing families.

decay_db.label: decay
decay_db.short: Fall across the IR when the envelope is set to decay.
decay_db.long: An exponential envelope is what a real diffuse field's decay looks like, as opposed to the flat or windowed shapes.

crossovers.label: crossovers
crossovers.long: Exposed rather than hard-coded. Standard practice keeps bass coherent, because decorrelating low frequencies gives a vague, weak low end where the head does not shadow them. Whether that holds for a rotating field is open.

band_amounts.label: band amounts
band_amounts.short: Decorrelation multiplier per band, low to high.
band_amounts.long: Uniform values are exactly inert: bands are built as differences of lowpasses so they telescope back to the input, and the crossover colours nothing until it is actually used.

micro_delay_ms.label: micro delay
micro_delay_ms.short: Per-source delay spread. A cruder decorrelator, kept for comparison.
micro_delay_ms.long: Colours differently from velvet or allpass because it comb filters when the sources sum. Spread runs from 0 at the first source up to this value at the last.

micro_pitch_cents.label: micro pitch
micro_pitch_cents.short: Per-source detune spread. Another crude decorrelator.
micro_pitch_cents.long: Changes duration as well as pitch, so over a long segment the sources drift out of time with each other. That drift is the reason it is called crude.

lfo_hz.label: coherence LFO
lfo_hz.short: Rate at which the decorrelation amount is modulated.
lfo_hz.long: Coherence that breathes rather than sitting still. Distinct from the hotspot, which moves coherence around the ring rather than pulsing it everywhere at once.

lfo_depth.label: LFO depth
lfo_depth.short: How far the coherence LFO swings the amount.

lfo_source_spread.label: LFO spread
lfo_source_spread.short: Phase offset of the LFO across sources. 0 is all in phase.
lfo_source_spread.long: At 1 the modulation is spread over a full cycle around the ring, which approaches a hotspot travelling at the LFO rate.

hotspot.enabled.label: hotspot
hotspot.enabled.short: Makes coherence a property of a direction rather than of a source.
hotspot.enabled.long: The sharpest form of the hypothesis. With per-source amounts the coherent source travels with the ring, so there is still a trajectory to follow. Here the hotspot sweeps on its own and a source is coherent only while it is near it. Set the ring rate to 0 and this rate to nonzero and no source moves at all while the coherence structure rotates: rotation carried purely by aggregate interaural statistics.

hotspot.deg_per_sec.label: hotspot rate
hotspot.deg_per_sec.short: How fast the coherent region sweeps around the ring.
hotspot.deg_per_sec.long: Independent of the ring rate, including opposite in sign.

hotspot.width_deg.label: hotspot width
hotspot.width_deg.short: Angular width of the coherent region.
hotspot.width_deg.long: Wide enough and every source is partly coherent at once, which removes the point of it. Narrow enough and only one source at a time is affected, which approaches the per-source case.

hotspot.hot_amount.label: hot amount
hotspot.hot_amount.short: Decorrelation amount at the centre of the hotspot. Usually 0, meaning coherent.

hotspot.bed_amount.label: bed amount
hotspot.bed_amount.short: Decorrelation amount far from the hotspot. Usually 1, meaning fully diffuse.

hotspot.shape.label: hotspot shape
hotspot.shape.short: Falloff from centre to bed: gaussian or cosine.
hotspot.shape.long: Cosine reaches the bed value exactly at the stated width. Gaussian never quite does, so its effective width is wider than the number suggests.

seed.label: seed
seed.short: Fixes the random draws for the decorrelating filters.
seed.long: Not cosmetic. Coherence measurements carry roughly 0.05 of draw-to-draw noise, so two conditions compared under different seeds can differ by more than either control does. Fix the seed when comparing, or average over several.

block.label: block size
block.short: Overlap-add block for the time-varying convolution.
block.long: Sets how often the azimuth and coherence are updated. Larger blocks are cheaper and coarser; the Hann windows satisfy COLA at 50 percent overlap so the crossfade itself is transparent.

match.label: level match
match.short: How treated regions are matched to dry ones: lufs, rms, or none.
match.long: Matching is local, against the same passage played dry, so the song keeps its own dynamics instead of every region being flattened to the whole-track average. K-weighted rather than raw RMS because the decorrelation methods differ in spectral balance.

dry_mono.label: mono dry
dry_mono.short: Play dry regions as the same mono sum the spatializer receives.
dry_mono.long: On by default. With it off you are comparing the record's own stereo image against a field built from its mono sum, which moves two variables at once. The mono version is loudness-matched to the original, so toggling this does not change level.

iacc.label: IACC
iacc.short: Interaural cross-correlation coefficient, peak over plus or minus 1 ms.
iacc.long: Near 1 means coherent and tightly localized. Near 0 means diffuse and enveloping. It is the objective counterpart to what you are listening for, not a substitute for it: velvet measures much lower than allpass yet is heard as quieter rather than wider, and ring geometry barely moves it even where it may be clearly audible.

iacc_sd.label: IACC spread
iacc_sd.short: Standard deviation of the windowed IACC series within one render.
iacc_sd.long: The floor below which a difference in the broadband number means nothing. Several controls move IACC by less than this, and at full decorrelation the draw-to-draw spread across seeds is about 0.04 on its own.

iacc_bands.label: IACC by band
iacc_bands.short: IACC in octave bands from 125 Hz to 8 kHz.
iacc_bands.long: Shows where the coherence went, which the broadband number hides. The low bands are where decorrelation costs you: no head shadow means no ILD to carry a position, so a decorrelated low end reads as vague and weak rather than wide.

iacc_series.label: IACC over time
iacc_series.short: IACC measured in successive short windows.
iacc_series.long: A rotating field should modulate this cyclically. A static field with the same broadband IACC will not, which is one of the few places the metric can distinguish rotation from mere diffuseness.

lufs.label: loudness
lufs.long: Frequency weighted, so it tracks what you hear when the decorrelation method changes the spectral balance. Raw RMS misses exactly that.

coherence_matrix.label: measured coherence
coherence_matrix.short: Pairwise correlation actually achieved between the source signals.
coherence_matrix.long: The controls say what was asked for; this says what was got. They come apart often enough to be worth showing side by side.

rotation_signature.label: rotation
rotation_signature.short: Cyclic modulation of the interaural statistics at the rotation rate, measured against a matched static control.
rotation_signature.long: Broadband IACC cannot distinguish a rotating field from a static diffuse one: both can land on the same value. Rotation should instead show up as the interaural statistics varying cyclically. That measure is confounded on its own, because a song's own periodicity lands in the same part of the series. Measured on a 20 s passage, a completely static field scored 2.04 where genuinely rotating fields scored 2.65 to 3.14, so the raw number proves nothing. Only the difference against an identical configuration with every rate set to zero is interpretable, and a delta near zero means no measurable signature, which given finding 7 is not the same as inaudible.

findings.degenerate_ring: A fully coherent, evenly spaced ring renders with left and right identical to machine precision. It is a dead-centre mono image carrying no interaural information, and rotating it changes nothing. Symmetry-breaking is mandatory: decorrelation, uneven spacing, per-source gain, or per-source coherence.
findings.antipodal: Odd source counts avoid antipodal cancellation. With an even ring every source has one directly opposite it, and those pairs are what cancel.
findings.front_back: The analytic HRTF has zero front-back discrimination: azimuth 0 and 180 produce bit-identical HRIRs. A full lap therefore reads as left-right oscillation at twice the rate. Rotation direction is confounded; whether anything is pointable is not.
findings.level_preserving: Every decorrelation control preserves per-source level. A plain dry/wet blend dipped 5.4 dB mid-sweep, which would make the knob change loudness as well as coherence and render every comparison made with it worthless.
findings.local_matching: Level matching is local and K-weighted. Matching to the whole track's average flattens the song's dynamics, and raw RMS misses the spectral differences between decorrelation methods.
findings.sustained_material: Sustained material decorrelates far more readily than transient material. Theremin passages reach IACC 0.04 to 0.05 where guitar sits at 0.38 to 0.62. Transients hand the auditory system discrete localization snapshots, which is the percept being avoided.
findings.metric_vs_percept: IACC does not capture everything audible. Where the metric and the percept come apart is the interesting part, not an error to correct. Both are shown; neither overwrites the other.
findings.noise_floor: Coherence measurements are draw-dependent. IACC at full decorrelation varies by about 0.04 across seeds and inter-source coherence by about 0.05. Differences smaller than that are not resolvable from a single render per condition.
findings.density_saturates: Velvet density only does work while the IR is sparse. Past roughly 400 impulses/sec the IR is already noise-like and further density changes nothing measurable. IR length is the axis with real headroom.
findings.rotation_needs_a_control: No single render can show that a field is rotating. Broadband IACC does not separate rotation from diffuseness, and modulation at the rotation rate is confounded with the music's own periodicity: a static diffuse field scored 2.04 at 0.5 Hz where rotating fields scored 2.65 to 3.14. Every rotation claim needs a matched static control, identical in every respect except that nothing is moving.
